answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small stake before it may earn, like a cipher that opens only after slow key derivation: spawning thousands of fakes becomes expensive because each must fund its own bond. Reputation then accrues slowly, like nectar gathered flower by flower, and is non-transferable, so a fresh identity starts with nothing even in a vast, cold tundra of anonymous newcomers. An attacker splitting one budget across many fakes earns less than one honest agent, since each fake must re-pay the stake and re-earn trust from zero.
